producer_report.summary:
Drain now re-plans after every item (every group under drain_concurrent), using the same Drain::prepare and Plan::build_with that athena plan calls. Before, it built the plan once at the start and worked that frozen list. So a priority record added while a job ran, a job that ended, or a request queued meanwhile never reached it. Its skips went only to Report.notes, and an item it never reached got no line.

What changed:
- **Re-plan loop (drain.rs):** `drain_with` takes a fresh `steps.queue()` plus `prepare` before each wave. `batches_for` only filters the plan's groups by a `tried` set and never reorders. A `Carry` in the shared state keeps what a fresh queue view may lack: approved jobs and their plan entries, readings already made, and forced refusals. So nothing is approved, read or paid for twice.
- **Passed-over line (drain.rs):** `Drain::pass_over` writes `plan       <id> passed over: <reason>`, once per id per run. Item ends are logged from `finish`: not ready, held, skipped, over the budget or job limit, and stop. After the loop, a sweep logs refused, held, cyclic, and unreached items. An unreached item gets `run ended first: <stop>`, plus the shared path when it shares one with the last wave.
- **Clash path (plan.rs):** `shared_path` returns the clashing path by the plan's own overlap rule, and `disjoint` is rebuilt on it.
- **Read-ahead (drain.rs):** `run_parallel` now takes the wave plus the later batches of the same plan (used only to choose what to read ahead) and resets the pump each wave.
- **Tests (tests/drain.rs):** seven new tests. The two mid-run ones failed when I temporarily froze the plan, then passed again after I reverted that.
- **CHANGELOG.md:** a Fixed entry naming the causes, the re-plan and the log line.

Which cause hit drain-24 is not settled. The CHANGELOG names three: the frozen plan, drain approving proposals that plan does not, and a binary older than the dependency rules (found by reading).

fmt, clippy -D warnings, the policy scan and the full test suite all pass.

checks_run.note: all existing tests passed unchanged after the re-plan loop, before new tests were added

checks_run.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --locked --test drain -- passed_over replan priority_record drain_order
checks_run.note: 7 new tests pass; with the re-plan temporarily frozen (a mutation, then reverted) the two mid-run tests fail as intended
69 in-file tests (including batches_for) and 116 drain tests pass
84 plan tests, including the new shared_path test

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-cli: a test calling drain() with a priority record that lowers an urgent-text request shows that item is started after a higher-priority item. It covers both a record present before drain() starts and one added while an earlier item runs.
criteria_check.evidence: tests/drain.rs: `a_priority_record_that_lowers_an_urgent_request_puts_it_after_a_higher_priority_item` (record committed before drain) and `..._while_an_earlier_item_runs_still_puts_it_after` (record committed from the first run). Both call drain::drain over the real queue and plan (Replay wraps RealSteps) and assert the start order is U1, N, U2. With the re-plan frozen as a mutation, the mid-run test failed (U2 ahead of N); with the fix both pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a test builds one queue and shows the sequence of jobs drain() starts equals the entries athena plan's plan() returns for the same queue, including a group-1 item that has a cited-but-not-'Depends on' job id.
criteria_check.evidence: `drain_order_equals_plan_order` queues a refused request, an ordinary one, the newest request citing the refused id outside a Depends on line (asserted to be groups[0][0]) and a Depends on / Priority: high request. It asserts the started jobs equal drain::plan's plan.order. `drain_order_follows_the_plan_as_the_queue_changes` queues an urgent request while the first job runs, calls drain::plan then, and asserts later starts equal that order minus the running item; it fails when the re-plan is frozen.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-cli: a test shows each planned item that is not worked (held, refused, cyclic, not ready, clash with a running batch, over budget, job limit, run ended first) gets exactly one UI log line with its job id and a reason, once per run.
criteria_check.evidence: `passed_over_item_is_logged_once_with_its_reason` runs one drain::drain per scenario on Stub with Lines as the UI: refused, held, cyclic, not ready (needs_accepting), job limit (item and the unreached one), budget (item and the unreached one), stop requested, and a path clash. Each asserts exactly one line starting `plan       <id> passed over: ` with the reason text. It also asserts a clean run logs no such line. `a_replan_does_not_read_an_underspecified_item_twice` asserts one read and one underspecified line across waves. The clash scenario runs serially through the Stub, not through drain_concurrent. A job running beside it was not tested.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test: all pass, and the existing drain tests pass unchanged.
criteria_check.evidence: I ran all three: cargo fmt --all --check clean, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings clean, cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast no failures. Existing test bodies are not edited; Stub only gained two fields, a job_history override and a needs_accepting branch in run.

criteria_check.criterion: Grep of crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs and crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs shows drain takes its order from the same plan-building code as plan(), with no separate ordering in drain.
criteria_check.evidence: The only code that builds the drain's order is Plan::build_with, called in Drain::prepare, which both drain_with (first and every later plan) and plan() call. `batches_for` only filters plan.groups by `tried`; the in-file unit test `batches_for_flattened_equal_the_plan_order_and_tried_removes_only_that_item` asserts the planned batches equal plan.groups and plan.order. The remaining sort_by_key in drain.rs is the age order that feeds build_with, applied to put approved entries back in place.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry that names the cause found, the order fix and the passed-over log line.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] has a new Fixed entry: it names the frozen plan and notes-without-log-lines, the drain approving proposals that plan never does, and a pre-dependency-rules binary (found by reading); then the re-plan through Drain::prepare and Plan::build_with; then the `plan       <id> passed over: <reason>` line.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: reading.rs was not changed because no failing test pointed at plan_entry.

Departure from the plan: the clash scenario runs on the serial Stub with a stop, not through drain_concurrent. The detail is built from the last wave worked, which is what the sweep checks. The Sync stub was not used.

Departure from the plan: the mid-run tests use a `Replay` wrapper that delegates caps, queue, plan_entry and job_history to RealSteps, with read, run and landing faked. It is not the RecordingLander hook the plan preferred.

Departure from the plan: the plan said all the design points were read; the `Carry` stores approved items and their entries, readings and forced refusals as designed. Report.plan_groups and Report.refused still show the first plan, as before; Report.queued uses the last queue view.
The note `plan order contradicts priority` and the 'no room' note are now added once per run (note_once) so repeated plans do not repeat them.
With read-ahead on, each wave resets the pump, so a read-ahead thread now ends at each wave and restarts at the next. The in-file read-ahead tests pass unchanged; production leaves read-ahead at 0.
Which of the three causes hit drain-24 is not settled; the CHANGELOG names all of them.
mistakes: First draft of the `passed over` test helper matched lines with `contains(id)`; a one-letter id matched the word `passed`. Fixed by matching the `plan       <id> passed over: ` prefix.
learnings: Drain froze its plan: drain_with built `batches` once from the first `prepare` and ran them, while `plan()` rebuilds on every call. The base code does follow a static queue's plan order, so a static comparison test passes on it; only a mid-run change exposes the fault.
RealSteps::entry_of and reading::plan_entry already apply the latest priority record via job.priority(), so priority extraction needed no change.
A fresh `steps.queue()` from the Stub drops approved `job-of-...` items and the stub keeps listing landed ones, so the re-plan needs the Carry merge and the `tried` set.
The Bash tool here allows only cargo, git, ls, chmod, mv and rm: no grep, tail or wc.
desires: A way to run drain against the real fake-agent path with a mid-run hook; the Replay wrapper fakes read, run and landing, so the real run path is not exercised by the new tests.
The drain's start time for the 2026-10-30 drain-24 run, to settle which cause hit it.
